properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's idea, 2026-08-31. Nothing chosen.

THE QUESTION. "Eliminate redundant code" and "do it once" name one intent, but the design can see TWO different shapes here and their remedies point in opposite directions:

· DUPLICATION — the same logic written twice. Fix: MERGE. Nothing currently measures this; no tool in reflow2 reports it and no finding in the graph names an instance. It may be real and it is presently unevidenced.

· UNDER-SEPARATION — the build holding as one thing what the design holds as several. Fix: SPLIT. This IS measured, by `granularity_report`, today:
      art:service   crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs    10 capabilities  [unusual 5.88]
      art:detect    crates/reflow2-core/src/detect.rs     9               [5.18]
      art:temporal  crates/reflow2-core/src/temporal.rs   9               [5.18]
      art:heal      crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs        8               [4.49]
      art:graph     crates/reflow2-core/src/graph.rs       6               [3.09]
  against a median of 1 across 151 registered artifacts. service.rs is called out further: "No other artifact in this design realizes as many, so this is not the design's normal coarseness — it is one place that did not follow the rest."

🛑 AND THE TOOL REFUSES TO SAY WHICH SIDE IS WRONG, deliberately: N capabilities in one artifact may mean the artifact should be N files, or that the DESIGN over-decomposed and should hold fewer capabilities, or that it is right for this phase. That judgement is the user's. So the measured half of this question does not tell us to split anything.

⚠️ A REAL RISK IN CONFLATING THEM: a sweep briefed as "remove redundancy" that meets service.rs will merge or trim where the actual finding is that ten distinct capabilities share one file. That makes the coarseness worse while reporting progress.

📌 WORTH KEEPING AS A COUNTER-EXAMPLE OF DRY DONE RIGHT, already in this codebase: `sync_debt` borrows its judgement from `sync::assess_overwrite` rather than reimplementing it, and says so in its own record. Whatever this effort finds, that is the shape to preserve.

⚠️ AND A BOUND ON THE MEASURED HALF: `granularity_report` reads REALIZES edges only, so a file no Artifact points at is invisible to it — 141 files are in that state. It also measures NO SIZE at all: a six-thousand-line artifact realizing exactly one capability is silent here.
properties.name: OPEN — does "eliminate redundant code, do it once" mean MERGING duplication, or SPLITTING the five artifacts the build holds as one thing? The fixes are opposite
properties.no_relation_note: Searched "duplication same logic implemented twice do it once" and reviewed what the duplicate guard offered. Nothing in the design is honestly related: the nearest hits were about the near-match guard itself and about a skill-lint check, which share vocabulary ("twice", "same shape") and not subject. Notably, NO node in this graph records an instance of duplicated code — which is itself part of this question's content: the merge half of the target is entirely unevidenced, while the split half is measured by granularity_report. The one real neighbour is the sibling traversal question, and it links in from its own end rather than being duplicated here.
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm discipline — ideas as ideas. Anthony has not said which shape he means, and the two readings are both faithful to his words, which is exactly why it is worth asking rather than assuming.
